verdict: NEXUS wires the two orthogonal failure modes into one graded enzyme-health node with the three refinements. REFINEMENT #1 (soft AND): activity = folded_fraction(ΔΔG_fold) * bound_fraction(ΔΔG_bind), a product of two two-state equilibrium fractions in [0,1] — graded, not Boolean, so partial damage gives partial activity. REFINEMENT #2 (loss only): bound_fraction never rewards a mutation; no neomorphic-gain claim. REFINEMENT #3 (validate, don't assume) is the honest core, and it holds on MEASURED, NON-CIRCULAR data: on 808 SKEMPI interface mutations the two sensors are ORTHOGONAL — Pearson(predicted ΔΔG_fold, measured ΔΔG_bind) = 0.15 — so a stability-only node is BLIND to interface failures, missing 94% of the strong measured binding-breakers. Complex-held-out, classifying a real interface failure from the intrinsic sensor ALONE is near-chance (AUC 0.56); adding the EXTRINSIC sensor (flex_physics interface features) lifts it to 0.75 (+0.19) — the second sensor is what catches the failure the first is blind to, which is the whole 'you need both' thesis, measured and non-circular. HONEST BOUNDARY: the two SENSORS live in near-field STRUCTURE (the recoverable regime — that is why they work), and the soft-AND is clean logic; but the last link, activity -> FBA -> whole-cell phenotype, is the FAR-FIELD step this project repeatedly finds does NOT compose. The FBA demo makes that visible honestly: the two-state fractions SATURATE (a single mutation rarely fully unfolds a protein) and metabolic EXCESS CAPACITY buffers moderate loss, so only near-catastrophic damage moves flux — real physics, not a bug. So the metabolic step is a DEMONSTRATION of the wiring, NOT a validated phenotype predictor (that needs testing against measured IEM/essentiality). Net: the dual-sensor node is real and the orthogonality that makes it necessary is measured and non-circular; the structural half is trustworthy, the phenotype half is the honest open edge — exactly the structure-vs-dynamics split the whole project keeps landing on.
